tools.description: Talk to the WriteStack Coach (Quill), the user's Substack growth coach. It knows their notes, posts, stats, memory, and playbooks. Pass thread_id back to continue the same conversation. The reply is also saved as a Coach chat the user can open at thread_url. This spends the user's Coach allowance.

message.description: What to ask the Coach, in the user's words, plus any context they gave you.

thread_id.description: thread_id from an earlier ask_coach result. Pass it to continue that conversation. Leave it out to start a new chat.

tools.name: ask_coach

tools.description: Create a WriteStack article draft. BEFORE calling, call list_article_newsletters and ASK the user which newsletter this article belongs to, then pass that publicationId. Only enabled newsletters are accepted — never guess or pick a default. Also pass title or topic, optional subtitle, markdown body, imageUrl (remote images fetched to S3 and inserted), and an optional plannedForDate target date (omit for an undated draft). Images in bodyMarkdown are also fetched to S3. GitHub-flavored Markdown body. Supported and synced to Substack: headings #–######, **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `inline code`, [links](https://...), images ![alt](url), bullet and numbered lists, > blockquotes, :::pullquote ... :::, :::callout ... :::, and a paid-only split with a standalone :::paywall::: line (content after it is behind the Substack paywall). Voice and video embeds are not supported.

bodyMarkdown.description: GitHub-flavored Markdown body. Supported and synced to Substack: headings #–######, **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `inline code`, [links](https://...), images ![alt](url), bullet and numbered lists, > blockquotes, :::pullquote ... :::, :::callout ... :::, and a paid-only split with a standalone :::paywall::: line (content after it is behind the Substack paywall). Voice and video embeds are not supported.

imageUrl.description: Optional remote image URLs to insert into the article. WriteStack fetches each URL, stores the image on S3, and appends it to the markdown body. Markdown/HTML images already in bodyMarkdown are ingested the same way. Max 20. Pass full https:// URLs. Invalid or unreachable URLs are skipped. Images are uploaded to Substack when the article is opened or saved with the Chrome extension, and again when pushing the draft.

plannedForDate.description: Optional ISO target date to place the article on the calendar. Omit for an undated draft.

publicationId.description: Enabled newsletter publicationId. BEFORE creating or pushing an article, call list_article_newsletters and ASK the user which newsletter to use. Never guess or pick a default. Only IDs returned by that tool are accepted — newsletters the user hid from Articles are rejected.

tools.name: create_article

tools.description: Create multiple notes at once. Each note's content body must be in Markdown format. Each note can have its own status, tags, auto-restack delay (autoRestackAfterHours), link-preview choice (includePreviews), optional imageUrl (remote image URLs, max 5 per note — fetched and stored like CSV import), Buffer channels (bufferChannelIds), and per-channel Buffer posts (bufferChannelPosts). If any content includes a link, ask the user if they'd like link previews before calling this tool; pass includePreviews: true only for notes where they confirm. You SHOULD ask the user which tags to apply before calling this — use list_tags first to show available tags if needed. Tags also control which reserved queue times the notes can take when later scheduled (OR match; untagged notes only use open or untagged-only times). When generating new note content, call get_writing_style first unless the user already pasted complete style instructions. Call list_buffer_channels first if setting Buffer channels or per-channel posts.

autoRestackAfterHours.description: Optional auto-restack delay in hours (1–168). If set, after the note is published WriteStack will automatically restack (re-post) it the given number of hours later to boost visibility. Pass null or omit to disable auto-restack on the note. Requires the WriteStack browser extension v1.4.78 or higher to actually fire.

bufferChannelIds.description: Optional array of Buffer channel IDs to cross-post this new note to once it publishes on Substack. Call list_buffer_channels first to get the valid IDs — only IDs returned by that tool are accepted. Maximum 20 channels per note — requests with more are rejected. Channel IDs from bufferChannelPosts are merged in automatically. Omit or pass an empty array to skip Buffer cross-posting unless you also pass bufferChannelPosts. Requires a connected Buffer account. Platform limits still apply: Instagram requires an image or video, and Instagram feed images must be between 4:5 and 1.91:1 aspect ratio for automatic posting (otherwise Buffer falls back to Notify Me). See https://support.buffer.com/article/622-instagrams-accepted-aspect-ratio-ranges

bufferChannelPosts.description: Optional per-channel Buffer post overrides when a channel should have different text or images than the Substack note. Call list_buffer_channels first. Each item needs bufferChannelId and, unless reset is true, a plain-text body (max 5000). Those channel IDs are also selected on the note (merged with bufferChannelIds, still max 20). imageUrl attaches images to that channel only — they are not added to the Substack note. Omit imageUrl to keep existing channel images; pass [] to clear them. includePreviews adds a link card from the first URL in that channel's body (max 1). reset: true deletes the override so the channel falls back to the note. Removing a channel from bufferChannelIds does not delete a saved override. Platform limits still apply: Instagram requires an image or video, and Instagram feed images must be between 4:5 and 1.91:1 aspect ratio for automatic posting (otherwise Buffer falls back to Notify Me). See https://support.buffer.com/article/622-instagrams-accepted-aspect-ratio-ranges

body.description: Plain-text override for this channel (max 5000). Required unless reset is true. This is what Buffer publishes for this channel instead of the Substack note.

imageUrl.description: Remote image URLs for this channel only (max 5). WriteStack fetches and stores them. They are not added to the Substack note. Omit to keep existing channel images; pass [] to clear them.

includePreviews.description: If true, attach a rich link-preview card from the first URL in this channel's body. Max 1 preview per channel.

reset.description: If true, delete this channel's custom post so it falls back to the Substack note. The channel stays selected.

imageUrl.description: Optional remote image URLs to attach to the note (same as CSV import image_url). WriteStack fetches each URL and stores the image. Max 5. Pass full https:// URLs. Invalid or unreachable URLs are skipped.

includePreviews.description: If the note's content contains a link (full https:// URL or bare domain like writestack.io), ask the user whether they want a rich link-preview card (image, title, description) attached before creating/updating the note - do not assume yes. If they confirm, pass includePreviews: true. Prefer writing links as full https:// URLs in the content so previews resolve reliably. Only one preview can be attached per note; if there are multiple links, the first link in the content is used.

tags.description: Category/tag names to assign. Tags also decide which reserved queue times this note can take: a note matches a reserved slot if it shares ANY of the slot's tags. Untagged notes only use open or untagged-only times. Call list_tags first to show available names.

tools.description: Return the link to the WriteStack features board, where the user can post a product or feature idea for others to vote on. This tool only returns the link: it does not submit, store, or send the idea anywhere, and you cannot submit suggestions on the user's behalf. Use when the user asks for functionality that is not currently possible in the MCP or app, then tell them to post their idea at https://writestack.io/features.

context.description: Optional extra context about why this is needed

suggestion.description: Short summary of the feature the user wants. It is not submitted anywhere; the user posts it on the features board themselves.

tools.description: Get the next N available posting slots based on your schedule template and already-scheduled notes. Pass tagNames to preview as if scheduling a note with those tags (first open or matching reserved lane; tagged previews skip untagged-only times). Omit tagNames to list the next free times in chronological order, including reserved and untagged-only times that are currently empty — do not assume an untagged note can use reserved times, or that a tagged note can use untagged-only times. Each result includes source (lane | open | any), the slot's tags, and untaggedNotesOnly. Call this before schedule_notes to preview when notes would be scheduled. Queue routing: each weekly time can reserve tags, accept only untagged notes, or stay open for any note, and may also set default Buffer channels. A time with tags is a reserved lane — it stays empty until a note shares ANY of those tags (OR). A time marked untaggedNotesOnly (and with no tags) accepts only notes with no tags; tagged notes never take those times, including Add to Queue leftovers. Untagged notes never take reserved lanes. When filling the next template times (schedule_notes), a tagged note takes the first open (any-note) time or matching reserved lane, whichever comes first. An untagged note takes the first open or untagged-only time. If a time has Buffer channels, those replace the note's channels when the note lands there (apply-on-schedule only). Substack still always posts. Call get_schedule to see each slot's tags, untaggedNotesOnly, and bufferChannels.

count.description: Number of available slots to return (1–100)

tagNames.description: Optional tag names to preview as if scheduling a note with those tags. Uses the first open (any-note) time or matching reserved lane, whichever comes first. Tagged previews skip untagged-only times. Several slot tags are OR — one shared tag is enough. Omit to list the next free times in chronological order, including reserved and untagged-only times that are currently empty — do not assume an untagged note can use reserved times, or that a tagged note can use untagged-only times. Call list_tags first if you need valid names.

tools.name: get_next_available_slots

tools.description: Get a single note by ID with its full content, including auto-restack configuration (autoRestackAfterHours), Buffer cross-post channels (bufferChannelIds), and any per-channel Buffer post overrides (bufferChannelPosts: custom text and attachments for a channel).

tools.description: Analyze the user's published Substack notes analytics: returns a paginated batch of notes with engagement metrics (impressions, clicks, reactions, comments, restacks, profile visits, shares, free/paid subscribers) and an audience split (subscribers, followers, strangers) when Substack stored one. audience is null when that note has no split. Not looked up by note IDs. Use when they ask to review note performance, compare top notes, find what drove subscribers, or summarize stats over a period. Filter by dateRange (or custom startDate/endDate), sort by orderBy/orderDirection, optionally search note text, and paginate with page/limit; check hasMore for the next page. Requires advanced statistics and a valid WriteStack extension key; on failure, read the error field for next steps.

dateRange.description: Time period for statistics. Use 'custom' together with startDate/endDate for an explicit range.

endDate.description: ISO 8601 end date for a custom range (sets dateRange to 'custom').

search.description: Optional free-text filter over the note body

startDate.description: ISO 8601 start date for a custom range (sets dateRange to 'custom').

tools.name: get_notes_statistics

tools.description: Read this writer's Substack post statistics for every newsletter selected on Posts Statistics, in one call. Returns views, unique email opens, Substack's reported open rate, emails sent and delivered, email traffic share, email-attributed views, likes, comments, restacks, shares, clicks, and signups, plus each newsletter's subscriber split and ARR. Open rate is unique opens divided by emails delivered. Use the returned openRate. Do not recompute it, and do not treat emailTrafficShare as the open rate: that share is the portion of views that came from email, including repeat views. Defaults to the last 30 days, highest views first. Omit publicationId unless they named one newsletter. Requires the posts statistics feature and WriteStack extension 1.5.25 or newer. On failure, follow the error text.

dateRange.description: Time period. Use custom with startDate and endDate.

limit.description: How many posts to return, highest views first (default 15, max 30).

publicationId.description: Limit to one newsletter by its Substack publication id. Omit to include every newsletter selected on Posts Statistics.

Each slot may list reserved tags (a reserved lane), untaggedNotesOnly (only notes with no tags), and default Buffer cross-post channels. Queue routing: each weekly time can reserve tags, accept only untagged notes, or stay open for any note, and may also set default Buffer channels. A time with tags is a reserved lane — it stays empty until a note shares ANY of those tags (OR). A time marked untaggedNotesOnly (and with no tags) accepts only notes with no tags; tagged notes never take those times, including Add to Queue leftovers. Untagged notes never take reserved lanes. When filling the next template times (schedule_notes), a tagged note takes the first open (any-note) time or matching reserved lane, whichever comes first. An untagged note takes the first open or untagged-only time. If a time has Buffer channels, those replace the note's channels when the note lands there (apply-on-schedule only). Substack still always posts. Call get_schedule to see each slot's tags, untaggedNotesOnly, and bufferChannels.

tools.description: Check how many more notes the user is allowed to schedule on their current plan. Returns maxScheduledNotes (the plan limit), currentScheduledCount, remaining (how many more they may schedule right now), and unlimited (true = the user has the Unlimited Schedules addon and there is no limit). Results are deduped by thread, include ancestor rows when needed, and each item includes merged attachments plus reaction/restack/comment counts. tools.description: Schedule notes to the user's next available posting slots based on their recurring schedule template. Each note is routed by its own tags: first open or matching reserved lane. Untagged notes only use open or untagged-only slots. You can also set or update each note's autoRestackAfterHours at the same time (1–168 hours; null clears it). To also cross-post the notes to Buffer channels when they publish, pass bufferChannelIds (call list_buffer_channels first to get valid IDs) — the same channels are applied to every note in the batch, except a slot with its own Buffer channels replaces those for the note that lands there. Queue routing: each weekly time can reserve tags, accept only untagged notes, or stay open for any note, and may also set default Buffer channels. A time with tags is a reserved lane — it stays empty until a note shares ANY of those tags (OR). A time marked untaggedNotesOnly (and with no tags) accepts only notes with no tags; tagged notes never take those times, including Add to Queue leftovers. Untagged notes never take reserved lanes. When filling the next template times (schedule_notes), a tagged note takes the first open (any-note) time or matching reserved lane, whichever comes first. An untagged note takes the first open or untagged-only time. If a time has Buffer channels, those replace the note's channels when the note lands there (apply-on-schedule only). Substack still always posts. Call get_schedule to see each slot's tags, untaggedNotesOnly, and bufferChannels. You MAY create notes without asking. CRITICAL: Scheduling in WriteStack does NOT push notes to Substack. After scheduling, the user must open WriteStack and click the yellow Sync/Warning button so the Chrome extension syncs them — you cannot do this for them. BEFORE calling this tool, you MUST ask the user to confirm they understand they need to sync manually afterward, then pass userConfirmedManualSync: true. Never set that flag unless they explicitly confirmed in this conversation. IMPORTANT: Call get_schedule_capacity first. NEVER, under any circumstances, schedule more than the reported `remaining` (unless unlimited=true). If the user asks to schedule more than `remaining`, schedule only the first `remaining` notes, leave the rest as ready/drafts, and tell the user how many were scheduled and why the rest were not. Scheduling sets the notes' status to scheduled and assigns posting times; this integration cannot unschedule them, so the user would have to undo it in WriteStack.

If set, after the note is published WriteStack will automatically restack (re-post) it the given number of hours later to boost visibility. Pass null or omit to disable auto-restack on the note. Requires the WriteStack browser extension v1.4.78 or higher to actually fire. When provided here, the same value is applied to every note in this batch. To set different values per note, call update_note for each one after scheduling.

Call list_buffer_channels first to get the valid IDs — only IDs returned by that tool are accepted. Maximum 20 channels per note — requests with more are rejected. When set, WriteStack will also post the note to these Buffer channels (e.g. LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Threads) shortly after it goes live. Pass an empty array or omit to leave cross-posting unchanged; pass the channels you want to keep, since this replaces any previously set channels. Requires a connected Buffer account. Platform limits still apply: Instagram requires an image or video, and Instagram feed images must be between 4:5 and 1.91:1 aspect ratio for automatic posting (otherwise Buffer falls back to Notify Me). See https://support.buffer.com/article/622-instagrams-accepted-aspect-ratio-ranges When provided here, the same channels are applied to every note in this batch, unless the slot the note lands on has its own Buffer channels — those replace the batch value for that note.

tools.description: Update an article's title, subtitle, markdown body, imageUrl (remote images fetched to S3 and appended), or Substack settings (audience, comments, SEO, slug, social title, publishAt). This saves locally only — it does not push to Substack. Pass baseVersion from get_article; a version conflict means you must re-read the article. Images in bodyMarkdown are fetched to S3. Body markdown supports the same Substack-safe formats as create_article (headings, bold/italic/strike/code, lists, quotes, pullquotes, callouts, paywall, links, images). BEFORE calling this tool, you MUST call get_article for the same articleId and base the update on that fresh copy — the user may have edited the article in WriteStack. Never update from a stale draft you wrote earlier in the conversation. Replaces the article's current content and settings with the values you pass; there is no undo through this integration.

baseVersion.description: contentVersion from get_article. Pass it to avoid overwriting newer edits.

bodyMarkdown.description: GitHub-flavored Markdown body. Supported and synced to Substack: headings #–######, **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `inline code`, [links](https://...), images ![alt](url), bullet and numbered lists, > blockquotes, :::pullquote ... :::, :::callout ... :::, and a paid-only split with a standalone :::paywall::: line (content after it is behind the Substack paywall). Voice and video embeds are not supported.

imageUrl.description: Optional remote image URLs to insert into the article. WriteStack fetches each URL, stores the image on S3, and appends it to the markdown body. Markdown/HTML images already in bodyMarkdown are ingested the same way. Max 20. Pass full https:// URLs. Invalid or unreachable URLs are skipped. Images are uploaded to Substack when the article is opened or saved with the Chrome extension, and again when pushing the draft.

tools.name: update_article

tools.description: Update an existing note's content, status, tags, auto-restack delay (autoRestackAfterHours), Buffer cross-post channels (bufferChannelIds), per-channel Buffer posts (bufferChannelPosts), or link preview (includePreviews). The content body must be in Markdown format. If the resulting content includes a link, ask the user if they'd like a link preview before calling this tool; pass includePreviews: true only if they confirm. Pass autoRestackAfterHours: null to disable auto-restack on a note that previously had it. To set Buffer channels, call list_buffer_channels first and pass bufferChannelIds (empty array clears them). To give a channel different text or images than the Substack note, pass bufferChannelPosts. Changing tags changes which reserved queue times the note can take if it is scheduled later. Overwrites the current value of each field you pass; this integration has no undo, so call get_note first and confirm with the user before replacing existing content.

autoRestackAfterHours.description: Optional auto-restack delay in hours (1–168). If set, after the note is published WriteStack will automatically restack (re-post) it the given number of hours later to boost visibility. Pass null or omit to disable auto-restack on the note. Requires the WriteStack browser extension v1.4.78 or higher to actually fire.

bufferChannelIds.description: Optional array of Buffer channel IDs to cross-post this note to once it publishes on Substack. Call list_buffer_channels first to get the valid IDs — only IDs returned by that tool are accepted. Maximum 20 channels per note — requests with more are rejected. Omit to leave cross-posting unchanged; pass an empty array to clear/disable Buffer cross-posting; pass the channel IDs you want (this replaces any previously set channels). Channel IDs from bufferChannelPosts are merged in automatically. Requires a connected Buffer account. Platform limits still apply: Instagram requires an image or video, and Instagram feed images must be between 4:5 and 1.91:1 aspect ratio for automatic posting (otherwise Buffer falls back to Notify Me). See https://support.buffer.com/article/622-instagrams-accepted-aspect-ratio-ranges

bufferChannelPosts.description: Optional per-channel Buffer post overrides when a channel should have different text or images than the Substack note. Call list_buffer_channels first. Each item needs bufferChannelId and, unless reset is true, a plain-text body (max 5000). Those channel IDs are also selected on the note (merged with bufferChannelIds, still max 20). imageUrl attaches images to that channel only — they are not added to the Substack note. Omit imageUrl to keep existing channel images; pass [] to clear them. includePreviews adds a link card from the first URL in that channel's body (max 1). reset: true deletes the override so the channel falls back to the note. Removing a channel from bufferChannelIds does not delete a saved override. Platform limits still apply: Instagram requires an image or video, and Instagram feed images must be between 4:5 and 1.91:1 aspect ratio for automatic posting (otherwise Buffer falls back to Notify Me). See https://support.buffer.com/article/622-instagrams-accepted-aspect-ratio-ranges

body.description: Plain-text override for this channel (max 5000). Required unless reset is true. This is what Buffer publishes for this channel instead of the Substack note.

imageUrl.description: Remote image URLs for this channel only (max 5). WriteStack fetches and stores them. They are not added to the Substack note. Omit to keep existing channel images; pass [] to clear them.

includePreviews.description: If true, attach a rich link-preview card from the first URL in this channel's body. Max 1 preview per channel.

reset.description: If true, delete this channel's custom post so it falls back to the Substack note. The channel stays selected.

contentJson.description: New note body JSON, as a tiptap JSON string. Not a must, recommended only for fixes where updating the content doesn't work. Read a few jsonBody examples of published notes first to get an idea of the format.

includePreviews.description: If the note's content contains a link (full https:// URL or bare domain like writestack.io), ask the user whether they want a rich link-preview card (image, title, description) attached before creating/updating the note - do not assume yes. If they confirm, pass includePreviews: true. Prefer writing links as full https:// URLs in the content so previews resolve reliably. Only one preview can be attached per note; if there are multiple links, the first link in the content is used.

tags.description: Replace all tags with these category names. Tags also decide which reserved queue times this note can take: a note matches a reserved slot if it shares ANY of the slot's tags. Untagged notes only use open or untagged-only times. Call list_tags first to show available names.
